traceability.notes:
All requirements and acceptance criteria for story 024.0-DEV-IGNORE-INLINE-CODE-REFS are implemented and verified:
- **Core Functionality / REQ-IGNORE-INLINE-CODE**: `normalizeCommentLine` removes all backtick-wrapped segments using `/`[^`]*`/g`, ensuring inline-code `@story`, `@req`, and `@supports` are ignored. Tests assert no annotation tokens remain when they are only inside backticks. - **REQ-PRESERVE-BOUNDARIES**: The replacement uses `" ".repeat(match.length)`, preserving string length and thus character/word boundaries; tests verify exact expected strings (with spaces) such as "`@story` + `@req` docs" → " + docs". - **Common Patterns**: Tests cover documentation patterns like "`@story` + `@req`" and sentences with "using `@supports`" and confirm they do not produce detectable annotations. - **Real Annotations Detected**: A mixed case test with both backtick-wrapped `@supports` and a real `@story` annotation confirms that after normalization, only the real annotation remains and is surfaced correctly. - **REQ-CENTRALIZED-FILTER**: The behavior is implemented in `normalizeCommentLine` inside `valid-annotation-format-internal.ts`, which is the shared normalization helper used by the annotation-format rule. The file-level `@supports` annotation explicitly ties this function to REQ-IGNORE-INLINE-CODE / REQ-PRESERVE-BOUNDARIES / REQ-CENTRALIZED-FILTER. - **Multi-Line Support**: `normalizeCommentLine` operates on a single string line and is pure and line-agnostic. Since it is called per line of multi-line comments, the backtick filtering applies regardless of which line contains the inline code. There are tests for multiple inline-code spans on one line and for ordinary (non-backtick) annotation lines, which demonstrates the intended per-line semantics. - **No Regression**: The full Jest test suite (`npm test -- --verbose`) passes, including the new tests for this story, indicating no regressions. - **Documentation AC**: The JSDoc comment on `normalizeCommentLine` documents that it "strips any inline code spans wrapped in backticks (replacing them with spaces of equal length to preserve character boundaries)" and explains that it detects `@story`, `@req`, and `@supports` tags, which satisfies the requirement to document the normalization/backtick-filtering behavior.
Given the concrete implementation, targeted tests mapped to the story requirements, and a passing full test run, this story is fully implemented.
